Locked-room mysteries rely on mechanical locks and physical barriers without advanced security systems

surface_summary: Sanford Embury is found mysteriously dead in his locked bedroom with no apparent cause. Suspicion falls on his wife Eunice due to marital tensions and the presence of a poison dropper in her bathroom. The case involves a locked-room mystery with multiple suspects and conflicting alibis.
accepted_facts: Sanford Embury died suddenly in his locked bedroom
No external signs of violence or forced entry were found
A medicine dropper containing henbane poison was found in the bathroom
Only Eunice Embury and Aunt Abby Ames had access to the locked suite
inferred_conclusions: Eunice Embury poisoned her husband out of financial frustration
Aunt Abby Ames was hypnotized and accidentally administered the poison
Alvord Hendricks had a perfect alibi and could not have been involved
mechanism_description: The murderer hired Willy Hanlon, a performer training as a human fly, to climb the exterior of the apartment building and enter through Aunt Abby Ames' window. Hanlon silently traversed the locked suite, administered henbane poison into Sanford Embury's ear while he slept, and exited the same way. The poison caused sudden death with no external signs, and the medicine dropper was accidentally dropped near Aunt Abby's bed during the escape.
delivery_path: Alvord Hendricks hires Willy Hanlon to kill Sanford Embury
Hanlon climbs the exterior of the apartment building as a human fly
Hanlon enters through Aunt Abby Ames' window into the locked suite
Hanlon administers henbane poison into Embury's ear while he sleeps
Hanlon accidentally drops the poison dropper near Aunt Abby's bed
Hanlon exits the suite the same way he entered
Embury dies suddenly from the poison with no external marks
outcome_result: Alvord Hendricks is arrested and convicted for orchestrating Sanford Embury's murder through Willy Hanlon.

false_assumption.statement: Eunice Embury, the wife, is the murderer due to motive and opportunity.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Eunice had frequent quarrels with her husband and lacked personal cash, providing a plausible motive. The locked room and presence of the poison dropper in her bathroom suggest opportunity.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The real murderer used an external agent to bypass the locked doors, and the poison dropper was accidentally left behind by the killer, not Eunice.

supporting_points: She had a motive due to financial frustrations and quarrels
The poison dropper was found in her bathroom
She was present in the locked suite with the victim
Her behavior was defensive and angry when accused
false_solution.the_one_flaw: The locked doors and windows made it impossible for her to have administered the poison without detection, and the real killer had an external means of entry.

red_herrings.description: Aunt Abby Ames confesses to the murder under supposed hypnotism, suggesting she was the killer.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Her confession was false, made to protect Eunice, and she was not responsible for the murder.

red_herrings.description: Mason Elliott is suspected due to his secret love for Eunice and possible jealousy.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: He had a strong alibi and no opportunity to commit the crime.

closed_circle.rationale: The locked bedroom suite was accessible only to these individuals, and no external entry was possible through windows or doors.

bridge party duration for Eunice's alibi

inference_path.observation: Henbane poison was administered through the victim's ear
inference_path.correction: The poison was delivered using a medicine dropper during sleep
inference_path.effect: Explains cause of death and method of murder

Medicine dropper found in bathroom with henbane residue

discriminating_test.design: Reenact the locked-room conditions by securing the bedroom doors with the same snap-locks and observing if any person can enter or exit without unlocking. Additionally, test the possibility of entry through the window by a skilled climber simulating Hanlon's human fly technique. Observe if any physical traces such as raspberry jam or gasoline odor can be replicated during the entry and exit.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test reveals that no one inside the locked doors could have administered the poison, and that entry through the window by a climber is feasible and explains the physical evidence.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Successful demonstration that the window entry is possible and that the locked doors prevent any other access or egress.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is provided with all necessary clues including the locked doors, the poison dropper, the presence of raspberry jam and gasoline odor, and the knowledge of Hanlon's climbing skills. The alibis and motives of suspects are clearly stated, and the suspicious perfect alibi is highlighted. The confession of Hanlon and the connection to Hendricks are foreshadowed. The reader could deduce the true mechanism by questioning the locked-room impossibility and considering an external entry via the window.
